The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Mostly green, intact leaf
- Irregular yellowish/pale patches, especially on the upper portion
- No distinct dark spots, no powdery coating, no gray mold
- Diffuse chlorotic/mottled appearance

This looks like it could be viral mottling (CMV), leaf mold, or spotted wilt. Let me check reference images across 8 classes.
CMV shows severe leaf distortion/shoestring — doesn't match the intact leaf shape. Let me check Leaf Mold.
This Leaf Mold reference is very similar to the test image — same setting (leaf on surface), same yellowish patches on green leaf. Let me check more classes.
TSWV shows dark ring spots/bronzing — doesn't match. Now Septoria.
Septoria shows small dark spots with lighter centers — doesn't match. Now checking Early Blight, Bacterial Speck, Powdery Mildew, and Verticillium Wilt.

Powdery mildew shows white patches, Verticillium shows edge yellowing + wilting — neither matches. Leaf Mold remains the strongest match. Using my 8th view to confirm with another Leaf Mold reference.

The second Leaf Mold reference confirms it — same presentation: single leaf on flat surface, irregular yellow patches on green background, identical setting and symptom pattern.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: single tomato leaf, diffuse irregular yellow/pale patches, intact leaf shape, no dark spots, no white powder, no necrosis
- **Leaf_Mold** (CDDM_1006, CDDM_1036): identical match — same image setting, same yellow chlorotic patches on green leaf
- CMV: leaf distortion/shoestring — ruled out
- TSWV: dark ring spots/bronzing — ruled out
- Septoria: distinct small dark-centered spots — ruled out
- Early Blight: severe browning/necrosis — ruled out
- Bacterial Speck: discrete black spots — ruled out
- Powdery Mildew: white powder — ruled out
- Verticillium Wilt: margin yellowing + whole plant wilting — ruled out
